anzsic_codes.name: Human Pharmaceutical and Medicinal Product Manufacturing

merger_description:
Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated (**Vertex**) proposes to acquire 100% of the issued shares in Crinetics Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (**Crinetics**) (the **Acquisition**).

Vertex is a US-based biotechnology company, listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol “VRTX”, that develops, manufactures and markets a range of pharmaceutical products for serious diseases. It currently has 7 approved products for the treatment of cystic fibrosis, sickle cell disease, transfusion dependent beta thalassemia, and acute pain (including 5 that are approved by the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) and supplied in Australia). It also has certain products currently in development stages for other serious diseases.

Crinetics is a US-based pharmaceutical company, listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol “CRNX”, that has a focus on discovering, developing, and commercialising treatments for endocrine diseases. Crinetics has one product on market in the US, Palsonify (paltusotine), a prescription oral medication used to treat acromegaly, a rare hormonal disorder. Palsonify is not currently approved or under review for approval by the TGA for supply in Australia. Crinetics also has a range of products currently in development stages in the endocrinology, endocrine-driven oncology and metabolic diseases spaces.

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and engagement with third parties.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• There is no horizontal overlap between the existing products
supplied by the Parties in Australia.
• There is no horizontal overlap between the therapies in the
early stages of development by the Parties.
• The merged entity will continue to face competition from
alternative developers and suppliers of pharmaceutical
products.
